t: This is Victoria Park, a large urban park, mostly in Tower Hamlets in East London, with a small part reaching into Hackney. It takes its name from Queen Victoria, who came to the throne in 1837 and reigned until 1901, longer than any monarch before her. Her sixty-three years defined the Victorian era, a period of industrial, political, scientific and military change, and of great expansion of the British Empire. So the park carries the name of the queen whose reign shaped the age in which so much of London grew.
